subject: social
title: Follow the Map
about: Using a map to get somewhere: north, south, east and west as ways to walk, the left and right sides of a map, between, next to and across from, reading the map key to know what a symbol stands for, and following a simple route. NC 1.G.1.2: symbols and locations on maps.
tip: Draw a quick map of your street with north at the top and ask him which way he walks to a friend's house.

cards.q: The park is north of the school. You walk from the school to the park. Which way do you go?
cards.note: North of means toward the top of the map.

cards.q: The library is east of the park. You walk from the park to the library. Which direction?
cards.note: East is the side where the sun comes up.

cards.q: North is at the top of the map. Which side of the map is east?
cards.note: When north is up, east is on the right.

cards.q: With north at the top, where is west on the map?
cards.note: When north is up, west is on the left.

cards.q: You walk east to the store. Which way do you walk to get back home?
cards.note: To go back, you go the opposite way.

cards.q: You walked south to the pond. Which direction takes you back?
cards.note: North is the opposite of south.

cards.q: You stand facing north. Which hand points toward east?
cards.note: Face north and east is on your right, west on your left, just like a map with north at the top.

cards.q: The slide is between the swing and the sandbox. Which one is in the middle?
cards.note: Between means in the middle of two things.

cards.q: The bench is next to the tree. Is the bench close to the tree or far away?
cards.note: Next to means right beside something.

cards.q: The post office is across from the school. What is between them?
cards.note: Across from means on the other side of the street.

cards.q: The map key says a green tree means a park. You see a green tree on the map. What is there?
cards.note: The key tells you what each symbol stands for.

cards.q: The map key says a wavy blue line means a river. You see one on the map. What is there?
cards.note: Blue lines on a map are usually rivers or streams.

cards.q: The map key says a little airplane means an airport. You spot one. What is there?
cards.note: Always check the key before you guess what a symbol means.

cards.q: To get to school, Leo passes the park, then the library, then the school. What does he pass first?
cards.note: A route is the way you go from one place to another.

cards.q: Leo's route: walk south two blocks, then turn east. Which way does he walk first?
cards.note: Follow a route one step at a time.

cards.q: A big thing that is easy to spot, like a water tower, helps you find your way. It is a...
cards.note: A tall tower, a big statue or a bridge can be a landmark.

cards.q: North is at the top. On the map, the lake is above the farm. The lake is which way from the farm?
cards.note: Above on a map means north when north is at the top.

cards.q: The store is two blocks away. The zoo is twenty blocks away. Which one is closer?
cards.note: Fewer blocks means a shorter walk.
